A : the graph describes work the app asked for, so this reports an authoring mistake, not a device failure. Catching the base type catches derive-time and record-time mistakes together.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.LifetimePlan**: Per-transient lifetime analysis derived from a : for each resource, the execution-order span over which it is live (first touch to last touch). This is the input the backend's transient aliaser needs to recycle memory across non-overlapping lifetimes — the classic "the G-buffer's memory is reused by the bloom mips once the G-buffer is consumed" case. Backend-neutral by design: it yields abstract spans and an overlap/alias query, but makes no placement decision (offsets, pools, real memory requirements) — that is the backend's job, because aliasing two images also needs an aliasing memory barrier at the hand-off, which only the backend emits. A resource declared but never used by any pass gets no entry (nothing to allocate).
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.LoadAction**: What happens to an attachment's existing contents when a pass begins rendering to it. With dynamic rendering this is the VkRenderingAttachmentInfo.loadOp; derivation picks it from the access and the resource's history (first write = clear, write-over-existing or blend = load).
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.MaterialStore**: Owns what is behind each handle: its ordered texture ids, its per-material parameter bytes, and — when it was created for a named technique — that pairing. A material is a bundle of neutral handles plus a byte block, so this is pure bookkeeping and is shared rather than reimplemented per backend; the GPU resources stay backend-side and the draw path resolves ids with zero per-draw allocation. The parameter block lives here as a plain CPU array. Backends stage it into their existing per-frame uniform ring during recording, so a material needs no GPU object of its own, no lifetime tracking, and no frames-in-flight hazard — and is just a memory copy.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.PassBarriers**: The derived synchronisation work for a single pass: the layout/hazard transitions to emit before recording it, and the load/store actions for its render targets. Backend-neutral — the Vulkan backend turns into vkCmdPipelineBarrier2 and into the dynamic-rendering attachment infos. It also carries the derived GPU debug-label nesting (): before recording, the backend closes open groups, opens each of , then opens the pass's own scope (closed after the pass). Diagnostic-only.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.PipelineCacheFile**: Where a backend's persistent pipeline cache lives, and how it is written. Backend-neutral because the policy is: the file is per user, per backend, and per device, and it is replaced atomically so a process killed mid-write leaves the previous cache intact rather than a truncated one.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.PngWriter**: Minimal, dependency-free PNG encoder (8-bit RGBA) for debug framebuffer captures. Uses the built-in for the IDAT zlib stream and a hand-rolled CRC-32 — no image library needed. Not optimized (filter type 0 on every scanline); fine for validation grabs. Pure CPU work over a byte span, so it is shared by every backend rather than copied into each.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.RecordValidator**: Checks each recorded draw against what its pass declared. Deriving the graph already rejects a declaration that contradicts itself; this catches the recording contradicting the declaration — binding a resource the pass never asked for, handing a mesh to a technique that fabricates its own vertices, pushing bytes no channel of the technique can carry. It is one implementation rather than three because it speaks only in neutral terms — a , a technique name, resource handles and byte counts — and never touches a backend type. That is also what makes the bulk of it testable without a device. Hot path. This runs per draw. Every scan is a manual for over : no LINQ, no lambdas, and in particular never , which is an iterator method and allocates (its allocation-free counterpart is , which collects ids rather than searching for one). The steady render loop must not allocate managed memory. This is where a backend's record-path policy belongs. The verb implementations themselves (*RenderContext.Verbs.cs) are deliberately left per backend and unshared: they are nearly all descriptor-set, root-signature and bind-group construction, and the only neutral part is a small geometry-source switch — an abstraction over that would carry more indirection than it removes. So when the three verb paths differ on a rule rather than on an API call, the rule moves here instead of the code moving anywhere.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.ResourceLifetime**: The execution-order span over which a resource is live: from the first pass that touches it to the last, measured in units. Two transients whose spans do not overlap can share the same physical memory — the basis of transient aliasing. The span is inclusive at both ends; a resource live at order k occupies that whole pass, so two resources that share any order overlap and must not alias.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.ResourceState**: The logical state a resource is in at a point in the frame — the backend-neutral stand-in for an image layout plus its associated pipeline-stage/access scope. Barrier derivation reasons purely in these states; the backend maps each to a concrete (VkImageLayout, VkPipelineStageFlags2, VkAccessFlags2) triple. Keeping the mapping in the backend is what lets the Vulkan and DirectX12 backends reinterpret the same transitions independently — the backend-isolation invariant.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.ResourceTransition**: A derived state change for one resource, to be realised as a vkCmdPipelineBarrier2 image memory barrier before the consuming pass. The backend turns into the barrier's old layout + source stage/access scope and into the new layout + destination scope. may equal — a same-layout barrier still orders a write-after-write or read-after-write hazard (memory/execution dependency, no layout change).
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.ScheduledPass**: A pass placed in execution order, carrying the prerequisite passes derived from its read/write edges. holds immediate prerequisites (the last writer for a read; the last writer plus all readers-since for a write) — exactly what barrier derivation turns into vkCmdPipelineBarrier2 waits. Transitive ordering is handled by the schedule's sort.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.ShaderBinding**: One descriptor-bound shader parameter, as the reflection sidecar declares it.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.ShaderBindingKind**: What a descriptor-bound shader parameter is, classified from its reflected shape and access. The categories a backend's layout builder switches on — read-only and read-write buffers are separate kinds because DirectX 12 binds them through different root-parameter types, a split Vulkan does not make but must not lose.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.ShaderBindingMap**: A shader's bindings grouped by the category the record path fills, each ascending by index: element k of is the slot the pass's k-th sampled input binds to, element k of is uniform slot k, and so on. This exists so a technique's descriptor layout and the code that writes descriptors into it read the same array. Both used to recompute "N samplers, then M storage images, then…" from counts, independently — which is how a layout and its writes could come to disagree about where a binding lived without anything failing to compile.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.ShaderBindingTarget**: Which compilation target's numbering a reflection's binding indices belong to. The shader build emits a reflection sidecar per target, and they are different index spaces for the same source: the SPIR-V pass honours the shader's explicit slots, while the WGSL pass lets Slang auto-number in declaration order and splits a combined Sampler2D into two slots. So the same parameter can be index 0 in one sidecar and index 3 in the other. An index is meaningless without knowing which — a backend that read the wrong sidecar would build a layout that looks entirely plausible and binds the wrong resources.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.ShaderReflection**: The descriptor-bound resource shape of a shader, read from the slangc -reflection-json sidecar that the shader build emits next to each compiled module. Every parameter is recorded with the slot the shader actually gave it (), so a backend builds its descriptor layout from real indices rather than assuming a category order the author had to hand-number to match. The per-category counts remain available as derived views, computed from the same array a layout is built from, so the two cannot disagree. The JSON is target-specific, not shared: see . Which target a reflection was parsed for is carried in and must be checked before its indices are used.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.ShaderReloadRegistry**: Tracks which techniques each shader backs, for hot-reload. A backend records every technique it defines here; when a watched shader artifact changes, the backend maps it to a logical shader name and queues it, and draining (on the render thread) replays each affected technique's descriptor through a backend-supplied redefine callback, bracketed by a GPU drain and a pipeline-cache reset. Pure bookkeeping over neutral descriptors — the file watching, the artifact-name parsing, and the GPU/cache work stay in the backend, behind the callbacks.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.SpirvDepthTextures**: Which of a shader's sampled textures it reads by comparison (Slang's Sampler2DShadow and SampleCmp), found in its SPIR-V. Neither Slang's reflection sidecar nor the SPIR-V types tell a shadow sampler from a single-channel one (Slang gives both the same image type, its depth "unknown"); what differs is how it is read. So this follows every depth-comparison sample (OpImageSample*Dref*, OpImageDrefGather) back through the loads, access chains and sampled-image constructions to the variable it reads, and reports that variable's binding. The desktop backends build their samplers from it; WebGPU reads the same fact from the WGSL it parses (texture_depth_2d, sampler_comparison). A comparison whose image can't be followed back to a bound variable (one stored into a local, chosen by an OpPhi or OpSelect, or passed into a function Slang didn't inline) throws rather than going unreported: its slot would keep a plain sampler. Kaldra's shaders read their samplers as globals, which a function body loads directly.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.StoreAction**: What happens to an attachment's contents when a pass finishes (the VkRenderingAttachmentInfo.storeOp).
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.TechniqueRecord**: A registered technique: the name it was defined under, the descriptor the app declared, and the the backend baked from its shader. A class rather than a struct so a registry lookup on the per-draw path hands back a reference instead of copying.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.TechniqueRegistry**: Every technique defined on an engine, by name. Backend-neutral and device-free, so the record-time checks that consult it are unit-testable without a GPU, and so a technique-name miss reports the same way on every backend rather than once per backend's own exception type. This does not replace a backend's pipeline cache. Those are keyed by baked content (attachment formats, blend state) and stay where they are; this is the one place a name is resolved.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.TechniqueShape**: What a baked technique can accept, in backend-neutral terms — the return of a backend's bake step and the input to the record-time checks. It exists so those checks live once instead of three times: every backend already computes all of this while baking, so returning it costs nothing and, unlike a second accessor the backend must remember to keep in step, it cannot drift from what was actually baked. Every size here is in bytes, matching reflection and the backends' own block constants. A constant buffer holds whatever struct the shader declared — matrices, integers, float4 rows — so a float count is the wrong unit to describe one. That the push API happens to take a ReadOnlySpan<float> is a property of the call, not of the buffer; convert at the call site.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.TextureUpdates**: The rules holds a texture to, shared so that every backend refuses the same updates with the same words. A backend reads the shape from its own store and asks here before it copies anything.
- **BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.Graph.TimingDecode**: Decodes GPU timestamp readbacks into per-pass timings. Collecting the raw timestamps is backend-specific (a query pool vs a query heap, with different valid-bit masking), but turning begin/end tick pairs into milliseconds and aligning them to the schedule's leaf passes is identical across backends, so it lives here.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.AnimationClock**: Advances active storyboards by the per-frame delta. Held by the and stepped once per from its deltaSeconds, so output is fully deterministic: tests tick synthetic deltas and assert the resolved value over time — no frame loop, no GPU. Each active storyboard tracks its own elapsed time; every tick it normalizes each child animation's progress (honouring /// ) and pushes the eased, interpolated value to the target. When an animation finishes, releases the target while leaves the final value in place. As in WinUI, a held value stays until its storyboard is stopped: a storyboard that has finished is no longer advanced, but is kept, weakly, for to release.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.AnimationTimeline**: A that drives one target property. The only needs to resolve the target, record where a run starts, push the current value and release the target on stop, so the non-generic base exposes just those seams and the declarative target; the typed value and the apply/release/read delegates live on , and binds a typed write of its own. Either way the target is written through typed writes — no reflection, no boxing.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.AnimationTimeline`1**: The typed animation: produces a at a given progress () and writes it through . reverts the target. Concrete subclasses (Double/Color/Point) implement and apply their own easing inside it. The target is either plus , which bind the delegates when the animation begins, or delegates set in code. As in WinUI, a run with no From starts at the value the target shows when it begins — including the value of an animation it takes over from.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.BackEase**: Back easing: overshoots slightly before settling. f(t) = t³ − t·A·sin(πt), where A scales the overshoot.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.BounceEase**: Bounce easing, as WinUI's: in the default a ball dropped onto the end value, bouncing times, each bounce times lower and shorter than the one before. Each bounce is a parabola; their widths form a geometric series whose sum, with half the last, spans the whole curve.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.CircleEase**: Circular easing: f(t) = 1 − √(1 − t²), a quarter of a circle. As in WinUI, t is clamped to [−1, 1], so the root is always real.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.ColorAnimation**: Animates an from to over the duration. Interpolation is component-wise in the authored colour space (a cheap, deterministic lerp).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.CubicEase**: Cubic easing: f(t) = t³.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.DiscreteObjectKeyFrame**: A key that sets its property to at , holding the value before it until then, as WinUI's DiscreteObjectKeyFrame.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.DiscreteValueAnimation`1**: Holds a property at one value while its storyboard runs, as a WinUI ObjectAnimationUsingKeyFrames with a single key at time 0 does: the built-in templates' visual states use it to show a state's brush. It writes the animation rung, so leaving the state releases it and the property shows its own value again. Code-only.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.DoubleAnimation**: Animates a scalar from to (or by ) over the duration. A null starts at the target's value when the animation begins; a null with a ends at From + By. Drives a float or double property.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.DoubleAnimationUsingKeyFrames**: Animates a scalar through a sequence of s. Each key's is normalized against the ; the value before the first key holds at its value, the value after the last key holds at its value, and each segment is lerped with the upper key's own easing. Keyframes are assumed to be in ascending order.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.DoubleBinding**: Binds a double animation to its target. Double animations author in double, as WinUI's do, while Vysara's own properties are float, so a double animation drives either, converting on write and read.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.DoubleKeyFrame**: One key of a : the scalar the animation reaches at (measured from the start of the animation), with an optional shaping the segment that ends at this key.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.EasingFunctionBase**: The base of the built-in easing functions. A subclass defines the raw ease-in shape in ; this base mirrors it for and splices the two halves for , matching WinUI.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.EasingMode**: Which end of an easing function is shaped.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.ElasticEase**: Elastic easing, as WinUI's: a spring, which in the default overshoots the end value and swings back and forth across it, settling as its swings die away. f(t) = r(t)·sin((2πn + π/2)·t), where n is and the envelope r is 's curve with as its exponent.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.ExponentialEase**: Exponential easing: f(t) = (eᵃᵗ − 1)/(eᵃ − 1), where a sets how sharply it accelerates. A negative exponent turns the curve over, so that it decelerates instead.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.FillBehavior**: What an animation does to its target when it finishes.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.IAnimationTarget**: Something an animation drives on an object: an animatable dependency property, or one of the element channels that animate a property which is not a dependency property. Resolved once when an animation begins.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.IAnimationTarget`1**: An of value type : read, write and release, unboxed.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.IEasingFunction**: Maps linear progress t in [0,1] to an eased progress.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.Lerp`1**: Interpolates from to : 0 gives , 1 gives , and an easing may push it outside that range. A dependency property with one is animatable ().
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.Lerps**: The standard linear interpolations. A dependency property of one of these types is animatable without declaring a , and tweens them without one.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.ObjectAnimationUsingKeyFrames**: Sets a property of any type to the value of each of its in turn, as WinUI's ObjectAnimationUsingKeyFrames: how a visual state collapses what it fades out, or shows a brush, a string or an enum member of its own. Nothing is interpolated, so it drives any dependency property, animatable or not. Each key's holds from its , measured against the as 's are, until a later key's; keys need not be in order. Before the first, the property holds the value it showed when the animation began. The values are written to the animation rung, so stopping the animation (leaving its visual state) shows the property's own value again. A of zero shows the last key at once, which is how 's snap, with transitions off, shows it too. The XAML generator sets the duration to the last key's time when markup gives none, as WinUI does; built in code, set it so. The target is and . Each value must be of the property's type, or null where it takes null: the generator converts them at compile time, as it does a setter's, and one that is not is an when the animation begins, as is a value the property's own validation refuses. The values are held as objects but written unboxed, so a running animation, and beginning one again, allocates nothing.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.ObjectBinding**: An bound to its target, made by the target () when the animation first begins. The key values, which the animation holds as objects, are written to the target's typed property unboxed, and the value the target showed when a run began is held typed, so neither a frame nor a begin allocates.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.ObjectKeyFrame**: One key of an : the its property takes at , measured from the start of the animation. As in WinUI, the only kind is : a value of any type cannot be interpolated, only set.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.PointAnimation**: Animates a from to over the duration.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.PowerEase**: Power easing: f(t) = tᵖ, where p need not be whole.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.PropertyPath**: What a storyboard animation drives on its target: a dependency property of the target, or one reached through properties whose values are objects, as in WinUI's (UIElement.RenderTransform).(CompositeTransform.TranslateX) or (Border.Background).(SolidColorBrush.Color). The XAML generator resolves a Storyboard.TargetProperty path to one of these at compile time; the steps are walked when the animation begins, and a step may name a more derived type than the property before it holds (a SolidColorBrush property of a Brush), as long as the object found is one.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.QuadraticEase**: Quadratic easing: f(t) = t².
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.QuarticEase**: Quartic easing: f(t) = t⁴.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.QuinticEase**: Quintic easing: f(t) = t⁵.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.RepeatBehavior**: How many times a repeats: a finite iteration or . The default (default(RepeatBehavior)) is a single iteration.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.SineEase**: Sine easing: f(t) = 1 − sin((1 − t)·π/2), a quarter of a sine wave. Its is half a cosine wave, (1 − cos(πt))/2, with no sudden change in speed at either end.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.Storyboard**: A group of timelines begun and stopped as a unit — the thing runs and swaps per state. Children are the per-property s; the clock advances each by the storyboard's elapsed time.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.Timeline**: The base of everything an advances: a span of animated time with a , a offset, repeat/reverse behaviour, and a fill rule for what happens when it ends. Plain authoring data — the clock owns the running state.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.VisualState**: One named look a control can be in — e.g. Normal, PointerOver, Pressed. Entering the state runs its (a null storyboard is the resting/default look).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.VisualStateGroup**: A set of mutually exclusive s — e.g. the CommonStates group (Normal/PointerOver/Pressed). Exactly one state in a group is current at a time; entering a new one stops the previous state's storyboard. Groups are independent of one another.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Animation.VisualStateManager**: Drives a control between named visual states. The attached property carries the groups on a control's template root; starts the target state's storyboard, then stops the current state's. When the control is attached to a host its animates the transition; when detached (or useTransitions is false) the target state's end values are applied synchronously so headless tests still observe the result. As in WinUI, leaving a state releases what it set, whether its storyboard is still running or has finished, except a property the state entered animates too.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.BrushTransition**: Animates an element's background from one brush to the next when its Background changes, as WinUI's BrushTransition: set it as a Border's, Panel's or ContentPresenter's BackgroundTransition. A change from one to another animates, its colour (opacity included) interpolating over on the host's animation clock; so, as a Vysara extension, does a change between a solid colour and no brush, which fades the colour in or out. Any other change, and any change while the element is not in a live tree, shows at once. A change that arrives mid-transition starts the next one from the colour on screen.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionBrush**: Paint for composition content: what fills a or its border, or colours a . Named after WinUI's composition brushes: a solid colour (), a linear gradient () or an image (). The compositor switches on the concrete type, with no reflection. Paint is retained and mutable, as content is, and versioned on its own: moves on every change to what the brush paints, while the content that holds it keeps its version. One brush may paint many contents: every element showing the same XAML brush shares that brush's one composition brush, so a recolour is one in-place write however many elements show it, and a compositor that keys work on what a content draws reads both versions.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionColorBrush**: Paints one colour, as WinUI's CompositionColorBrush.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionColorGradientStop**: One colour of a , at along the gradient (0 at its start, 1 at its end).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionColorSpace**: The space a gradient interpolates its colours in, as WinUI's CompositionColorSpace (its RGB members).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionCornerRadius**: The radii of a rectangle's four circular corners in its local units, clockwise from the top left as WinUI's CornerRadius orders them. A radius of 0 or less draws a square corner.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionFillRule**: How a path's overlapping figures and self-crossings decide what its fill covers.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionGradientBrush**: The colour stops and modes a gradient shares, as WinUI's CompositionGradientBrush; a places them along a line. Stops are kept ordered by offset, and two stops at one offset make a hard edge between their colours. Colours interpolate as premultiplied values, the way a GPU interpolates vertex colours. In that is linear light, which a compositor reproduces exactly by splitting the painted geometry where the stops fall and colouring the pieces' corners, with no ramp texture to clamp or quantize colours above paper white. In the interpolation is in the authored, sRGB-encoded values, which are not linear in the light the GPU blends, so each stop interval is cut into pieces sampled exactly at their ends. Between those ends the colour is the straight line in linear light wherever it is sampled, so polygons that share a point, such as the triangles of a shape, agree on its colour. sRGB interpolation is not defined above paper white, so there a stop's channels above 1 are drawn at 1, as they would be by any 8-bit colour; a colour animation that overshoots, or a stop set above 1, never stops the frame. Interpolate in linear light to keep colours above 1.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionGradientExtendMode**: What a gradient paints before its start and past its end, as WinUI's CompositionGradientExtendMode.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionLinearGradientBrush**: Paints a gradient along the line from to , as WinUI's CompositionLinearGradientBrush: the colour is constant across the line, and stop offsets measure along it.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionMappingMode**: What a gradient's points are measured in, as WinUI's CompositionMappingMode.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionPath**: A retained, versioned vector path: figures of lines and quadratic and cubic Béziers, with a fill rule. It is the neutral form a geometry takes in the composition layer, named after WinUI's CompositionPath: what the public tessellator reads, and what a foreign compositor renders natively. Elliptical arcs are stored as cubic Béziers of at most 45° each, whose distance from the true ellipse is under 0.0005% of its radius. It is mutable and retained like the rest of the composition content: rebuilding it with and the drawing calls reuses its storage, so a path that keeps its size stops allocating. Every change advances , which work derived from the path (a tessellation) is keyed by.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionStretch**: How a surface brush scales its image into the box it paints, as WinUI's CompositionStretch.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionStrokeCap**: The shape at the end of an open figure or a dash, as WinUI's CompositionStrokeCap.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionStrokeLineJoin**: How a stroke turns a corner, as WinUI's CompositionStrokeLineJoin.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionStrokeStyle**: How a path is stroked: thickness, joins, caps and dashes, as WinUI's composition shapes describe it (CompositionSpriteShape.StrokeThickness, StrokeLineJoin, StrokeMiterLimit, StrokeStartCap, StrokeEndCap, StrokeDashCap, StrokeDashOffset and StrokeDashArray), with the defaults of XAML's Shape. Dash lengths and the dash offset are in multiples of , as in WinUI. Retained and versioned like : every change advances , which a tessellation is keyed by, and setting a value equal to the current one changes nothing.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionSurfaceBrush**: Paints an image, as WinUI's CompositionSurfaceBrush: is scaled into the box painted by and placed by the alignment ratios. Only the box is painted: an image that overhangs it is cut at its edges, and one that does not fill it leaves the rest transparent.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionSweepDirection**: Which way an arc turns from its start to its end, in a y-down space.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.CompositionTextAlignment**: How each line of a sits across its width, with the members and values of XAML's TextAlignment. Text is laid out left to right only, so is and is . Whitespace at the end of a line hangs past where the line is placed.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.ContainerVisual**: A grouping node with no content of its own.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.DrawListCompositor**: Kaldra's default : walks a surface's composition tree, folds transform/clip/opacity into a pre-transformed vertex/command stream, and exposes it as a neutral . Emits the rectangle family (fills + borders), MSDF glyph runs and vector shapes (, through the prim), painted by colour, linear-gradient or image brushes; a gradient is drawn exactly by cutting the geometry where its colour stops being linear (). Output is asserted on CPU via — the primary test seam, no backend needed.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.DrawListCompositor.RectShapes**: The outlines of a rect's rounded fill and of its border ring (the rect less its inner rounded rect, each of whose radii is the fitted corner radius less the thickness, as the rect prims draw it), for the rects drawn through the Vector prim. Kept on the content as its derived work, with their tessellations, and rebuilt only when the size, radii or thickness change.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.GlyphRunContent**: A run of laid-out text drawn from a . The compositor lays the glyphs out against through the atlas's shaper, with applied, emitting commands: the font and features the element measured the run with, so it draws in the space layout gave it. is in the visual's own units, as an element's layout is (DIPs); the transforms above it, the root's DIP→pixel scale included, take it to the surface. colours the glyphs, a gradient measured over . The text breaks into lines at its line breaks, each placed across 's width by . A run can carry two effects drawn from the atlas's true-distance channel, both sized in EM so they scale with the text: an outline (, ), the glyphs grown by the thickness, and a shadow (, , ), the glyphs moved and blurred. The compositor draws every glyph's shadow, then every glyph's outline, then the glyphs, so no effect lands on a neighbouring glyph. The field reaches / 2 past each edge, and an effect reaching further is drawn clamped to it; vysara:TextEffects validates the sizes it hands a run against the font.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.IDrawListSource**: An whose output is neutral draw lists. A hands out the list each surface's compositor last produced in , and tracks the texture sources it names (), whichever compositor produced it: , or a foreign one that implements this too. A compositor that renders some other way leaves it off, and its surfaces' lists are .
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.IUICompositor**: The portability boundary: renders a surface's tree. Kaldra ships ; a foreign engine substitutes its own and consumes the tree directly.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.LayerEffect**: A composition-tree post effect applied to a group's render-to-texture layer. A visual that carries an effect is always composited as one bitmap (exactly like a sub-1 group opacity), and the effect is applied when the layer is composited back into its parent. selects the effect the backend runs; .. are its parameters. Id 0 is the identity (opacity-only); id 1 is a Gaussian blur whose pixel sigma is .
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.PathFigureInfo**: Where one figure of a lies in its and , starting with its .
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.PathTrim**: The part of a path's stroke that is drawn, as WinUI's CompositionGeometry.TrimStart, TrimEnd and TrimOffset: fractions of the whole geometry's length, all its figures in order. The stroke runs from to , both moved by and wrapping past the end of the path back to its start, so animating runs a fixed-length piece round a path. Start and end are clamped to 0..1 and swapped when start is the larger; equal, they draw nothing. A trimmed stroke takes its start cap where it starts and its end cap where it ends. Trimming changes which part of a tessellated stroke is drawn, not the tessellation, so animating a trim never re-tessellates. It applies to strokes; a fill is not trimmed.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.PathVerb**: One drawing command of a , with the number of points it takes from .
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.RectContent**: A rectangle, optionally rounded, with a fill and an optional border: the Border, Panel and Image primitive. Each is painted by a : a colour, a gradient, or an image. Corners of their own radii, and an image on rounded corners or as the border, are drawn through the vector prim.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.RootVisual**: The root of one surface's composition tree.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.ShapeContent**: A vector shape: a filled and stroked, as WinUI's CompositionSpriteShape draws its geometry. The path is drawn through (a geometry's transform, a shape's stretch), which maps the outline but not the pen. The fill and the stroke are each painted by a : a colour, a linear gradient or an image, measured over . The stroke follows , and draws the part leaves. Retained and versioned like the rest of the composition content. The path, the stroke style and the brushes are retained objects versioned on their own, so a change made inside one of them leaves this content's alone; a compositor keying work on what the shape draws reads their versions too. The tessellations are cached here, keyed by the path (which object, and its version), the path transform, the stroke style's version and the scale bucket the shape is drawn at, so moving, fading, recolouring or trimming a shape never re-tessellates it, and the cache needs no lookup and is collected with the content. A foreign compositor reads the path, transform, paint and style and draws them natively, or takes the tessellation Vysara's compositor draws from and .
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.ShapeContent.CoverageProbe**: Finds whether any triangle drawn covers a point: the point inside it, and every edge distance interpolated there at least 0.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.SpriteVisual**: A leaf node that draws : a rect with its border, an image, a glyph run, or a vector shape.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.Visual**: A retained composition node — the tree a pluggable renders. Carries a 2D (animatable independently of layout), group , an optional , and a damage flag for incremental recomposition. Backend-neutral.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Composition.VisualContent**: What a draws: the rectangle family (fill + border, or an image), MSDF glyph-run text, and vector shapes. The compositor switches on the concrete type, with no reflection. Content is retained and mutable, like WinUI's composition objects: an element keeps one content object and updates it in place, so a brush change, an animation frame or a re-arrange allocates nothing. - **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.Popup**: A transient overlay: when is set, its is composited above the root's content at (, ) and hit-tested on top. The popup element itself occupies no layout space. With a full-surface layer behind the child closes the popup on an outside press. The popup must be attached to a live root (in the element tree) for to take effect; drives the overlay imperatively.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.Primitives.AnchoredPlacement**: Where something opened against an anchor goes (a tooltip, a flyout): on the side asked for, a gap clear of the anchor, turned to the opposite side when it would leave the bounds there and fits better on that side, and then slid along to stay inside the bounds. All in the root's DIPs.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.Primitives.EdgeAlignment**: How something placed beside an anchor lines up along that side: centred on it, or with its start (left or top) or end (right or bottom) edge on the anchor's.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.Primitives.FlyoutBase**: What a flyout is, as WinUI's FlyoutBase: something opened over the page against a target, by , a 's click or an element's . Its presenter goes in the target's root's overlay layer, on 's side of the target (turned to the other side where there is no room, slid along to stay on the surface, and no taller or wider than the room on its side, a presenter that scrolls scrolling), over a light-dismiss layer: a press outside closes it, as does Escape. Opening it focuses the first tab stop inside, and closing it gives focus back to what had it. One shows per flyout; opening it again moves it.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.Primitives.FlyoutPlacementMode**: Where a flyout opens against its target, as WinUI's FlyoutPlacementMode: on a side, centred on the target or with an edge lined up with the target's, turned to the other side where there is no room. is . , covering the window, is not provided: a flyout set to it throws as it opens.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.Primitives.FlyoutShowOptions**: How a flyout is shown, as WinUI's FlyoutShowOptions: at a point in its target (a context menu at the pointer), or against the whole target where is null; on 's side, or the flyout's own.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.Primitives.ListViewItemPresenter**: The whole look of a , as WinUI's ListViewItemPresenter: the item's built-in template is this one element, which shows the item's content inside over a background that follows the item's state. At rest it paints its own (the item's); hovered, pressed or selected it paints the brush its properties give for that state, faded by its , and a selected item's text takes where one is given. A state shows by the presenter swapping which brush it paints, with no storyboard per item. Disabled, a selected item shows and the text dims to the shared disabled brush, rather than fading the item, which Vysara's built-in looks never do. Not provided: WinUI's check mark and selection indicator, focus visuals, reveal, and DisabledOpacity.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.Primitives.ListViewItemState**: What a list item shows: whether it is selected, hovered, pressed and enabled.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.Primitives.Marks**: The small stroked marks built-in looks draw (a chevron, a cross, an arrow), each a of rounded strokes in a box of its own size.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.Primitives.PlacementMode**: Where a tooltip or a flyout opens against what it belongs to, as WinUI's PlacementMode: on the named side, turned to the other side where there is no room, or at the pointer.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.Primitives.Pressable**: The pointer and key handling a control that acts on a press takes from without being one (a toggle switch, an expander's header): whether the pointer is over its and pressed on it, and a primary press released over it, or Enter, Space or the pad's A while the control itself has focus, each acting once. A right or middle press is left alone, for a context menu. The control shows and in its CommonStates, told as they move.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.Primitives.SourceSubscription**: A control's hold on its items source's , taken only while the control is in a live tree, so a long-lived collection (a view model's) never keeps a removed control alive. Joining a tree again re-reads the source, since changes made while it was out were not heard.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.RadioButton**: One of a set of choices, as WinUI's RadioButton: a click checks it, never unchecks it, and checking it unchecks the others in its group, those sharing its under the same root, or with none, those sharing its parent. The built-in look is a ring with a dot while checked, beside its content; a template replaces it (a segmented row of toggles is a CheckStates template).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.RadioButtons**: A set of choices of which one is chosen, as WinUI's RadioButtons: a per item of (or ), shown through or as text, under an optional , in up to columns filled top to bottom, then left to right, as WinUI's. Choosing one sets and , dependency properties with change events, so they bind TwoWay. The set is one tab stop, the chosen button (the first while none is chosen); from it Up and Down (and the d-pad's) move the choice to the item before or after, and Left and Right to the next column. Items added before it is in a live tree, as markup adds them, are laid out once it is.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.ScrollBarVisibility**: Whether a scrolls along an axis and shows its thumb, as WinUI's ScrollBarVisibility. Vysara's scroll bar is a thumb alone, with no track, so shows as does: there is no thumb when there is nothing to scroll.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.ScrollMode**: Whether a finger panning a scrolls it along an axis, as WinUI's ScrollMode. It governs only panning: whether the content is laid out to scroll that way at all is the axis's , and the wheel, the keys and a thumb scroll whatever is laid out to scroll.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.ScrollViewer**: A clipping viewport over a single oversized , as WinUI's. Along each axis whose scroll bar visibility isn't (vertical by default, as WinUI's) it measures the content unbounded to learn its extent; it arranges the content offset by the scroll position and clips to the viewport. Scrolls by mouse wheel, by a thumb, by keyboard (Page/Home/End/arrows when a descendant is focused), by a finger where the axis's lets it, and programmatically; the offset is always clamped to /. A wheel it can't scroll any further is left unhandled, so an enclosing viewer scrolls instead. Pairs with , which reports its full extent for exactly this viewport.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.ScrollViewerViewChangedEventArgs**: A 's view moved, as WinUI's ScrollViewerViewChangedEventArgs. Vysara's scrolling has no inertia, so a change is never intermediate.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.SelectionChangedEventArgs**: What a selection change took away and added, as WinUI's SelectionChangedEventArgs: the items deselected and the items selected, in the order they changed.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.SelectionChangedEventHandler**: Handles a selection change, as WinUI's SelectionChangedEventHandler.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.SelectionMode**: How many items a allows selected at once.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.Slider**: A range control that picks a in [, ] by dragging a thumb along a track, clicking the track, or with the keyboard. The default template draws an unfilled rail, an accent fill up to the thumb, and a draggable thumb, and carries a CommonStates visual-state group (Normal/PointerOver/Pressed/Disabled) that the pointer drives. is coerced into range and snapped to on input; lets a {x:Bind Value, Mode=TwoWay} push edits back to a view model.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.Slider.SliderTrack**: The slider's visual: it lays out the rail (full length), the accent fill (up to the thumb), and the thumb (at the value's fraction of the usable travel) directly from the owning , so the geometry is recomputed on every arrange with no relayout feedback.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.StackPanel**: Stacks children end-to-end along : the stacking axis is measured unconstrained (∞), desired = sum along it and max across it; arrange lays children out one after another, each stretched on the cross axis.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.TemplateStates**: What the built-in templates' visual states are made of. As in WinUI's default templates, a state shows a brush of its own (a pointer-over or pressed background) by holding the part's Background at it while the state is current, and the resting state hands the background back to what the template bound it to, usually the control's own . The part's fades between them. Each state's brush is an on the property it holds, as WinUI's templates set one, so going from one brush to another hands the property straight over, and leaving a state releases its brush. The resting state is WinUI's empty one: going to it leaves the state that held a brush, which releases it, and a template being replaced leaves its states too (). A Disabled state swaps its parts' brushes for the disabled ones here, as WinUI's default styles swap in ButtonBackgroundDisabled, ButtonForegroundDisabled and the like, rather than fading the look: a faded part with children composes through an offscreen layer, and a disabled control inside another would fade twice. A brush is the same colour wherever it shows, so a check box in a disabled button looks as one disabled on its own does.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.TextBlock**: A run of text. Measures and emits glyphs against its root's font (, the embedded unless the host sets one) through that atlas's shaper, with the OpenType features its settings name, and hands the same font and features to the the compositor lays out into draws, so the run draws in the width layout measured. and are inherited, as in WinUI: unless set here (locally, by a style or by an animation), they are those of the nearest , or text block above, so the text a control's template or its string content shows takes the control's size and brush. The text breaks into lines at its line breaks and, with , at spaces to keep inside the width it is measured at; cuts a line still too wide short with an ellipsis; and places each line across the width the text block is arranged at.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.TextBox**: A single-line editable text field. Consumes the host's and events (the input pipeline already routes them to the focused element) to drive a caret + selection over : insert/overtype, Backspace/Delete, arrow/Home/End motion (Shift extends the selection), Select-All, and cut/copy/paste through a process-wide clipboard (an OS clipboard is a later host seam). is a dependency property with a event, so it participates in TwoWay {x:Bind}. IME is deferred — committed characters only.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.ToggleButton**: A that holds a checked state — the base for . A click cycles (two-state, or three-state through null when is set), raising // and driving the CheckStates visual-state group. Subclasses reflect the state in template parts via .
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.ToggleSwitch**: A switch that is on or off, as WinUI's ToggleSwitch: a pill-shaped track whose knob sits left when off and right, on the accent, when on, beside or , under an optional . A click, Enter, Space or the pad's A flips , raising ; lets it bind TwoWay. The track and knob take the ToggleSwitchFillOn, ToggleSwitchStrokeOff, ToggleSwitchKnobFillOn and ToggleSwitchKnobFillOff resources. Disabled, the track and knob take the shared disabled brushes, on or off, and the text dims.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.ToolTip**: The small panel shows over an element the pointer rests on: its , text or an element, on a rounded panel no wider than 320 DIPs unless its MaxWidth is set. It never takes the pointer, so what is under it stays hovered. A page recolours it with the ToolTipBackground, ToolTipBorderBrush and ToolTipForeground resources, as WinUI's lightweight styling does.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.ToolTipService**: An element's tooltip, as WinUI's ToolTipService: ToolTipService.ToolTip="Undo (Ctrl Z)" in XAML, or any element or . Once the pointer has rested on the element (or anything inside it without a tooltip of its own) for 0.6 s, the host shows it by the element's side; it goes as the pointer leaves, presses, scrolls or a key is pressed, and doesn't come back until the pointer leaves and returns.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.UIElementCollection**: The ordered child collection of a ; adds re-parent the child and invalidate the owner's measure.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Controls.VirtualizingStackPanel**: A vertical items panel that realizes only the containers intersecting its viewport. It assumes one uniform row height (, vysara:Virtualization.RowHeight in XAML), so the visible window is pure arithmetic from ; containers that scroll out are recycled back to the . It reports the full extent (ItemCount × row height) so an outer scroller sees the true size. It has no variable-height virtualization, scroll chrome, or wheel and scrollbar input: the offset is set directly.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.CornerRadius**: The radii of a rectangle's four corners in DIPs, as WinUI's CornerRadius, clockwise from the top left. Each corner is a circular arc of its own radius.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.DependencyObject**: The base of everything that carries dependency properties. Holds a sparse, int-keyed effective-value store and resolves the WinUI value-precedence ladder: Animation > Transition > Local > Template > Style > BuiltInStyle > Inherited > Default The Transition rung holds what a tween shows on its way to the local value it set, as a WinUI property transition shows it; a local change ends it. The Template rung holds what a {TemplateBinding} pushes onto a template part, so a Local value an app sets on that part wins over the template, as in WinUI. The BuiltInStyle rung holds what a control gives itself, the way WinUI's default style does: its built-in template, and that a control is a tab stop. An app's style or its own value overrides either, and a diagnostics read can tell them from the app's markup. A set recomputes the top of the ladder, coerces it, fires the typed change callback only when the coerced resolved value changes, and ORs the property's into the element (via ). A property WinUI inherits (a text property such as FontSize) then passes the new value down to the elements below that hold it, as their Inherited value. Reflection-free: dispatch goes through the typed delegates on . The store is typed: each property's rungs live in a slot of the property's own value type, made on the first write of that property to this object. After that a write, its coercion, its change check and its change callback never box, so animating a value-type property every frame allocates nothing. A field-backed property (Vysara's layout properties, such as Width) keeps its resolved value in a field of its owner, which a read returns. Its local value lives there too until a style, inherited or animated value makes it a slot, so an element whose layout only code or markup set holds no store at all for it.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.DependencyObject.ValueRung**: A rung of the precedence ladder below the default, highest first. holds what a tween shows on its way to the local value it set, as a WinUI property transition shows: below a storyboard's value, above every value set.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.DependencyProperty**: A reflection-free dependency property — the WinUI semantics (typed metadata, change/coerce callbacks, value precedence) with the -keyed, string-dispatched mechanism replaced by a dense integer slot () and typed delegates. Abstract base; the concrete property is always a . Identity is by reference.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.DependencyPropertyChangedEventArgs**: The data for a dependency-property change event such as : the property and its old and new values, as in WinUI.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.DependencyPropertyChangedEventHandler**: Handles a dependency-property change event.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.DependencyPropertyKind**: Whether a property is declared on its owner () or attached to arbitrary targets (, e.g. Grid.Row). Both share the one dense index space.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.DependencyProperty`2**: The concrete, typed dependency property.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Diagnostics**: What a diagnostics tool loaded into a running game builds on: the live hosts and their element trees, each dependency property's value and the level it came from, picking and bounds in surface pixels, a top-most overlay for the tool's own UI, run-time value parsing, and where each element came from in markup. Everything here is behind one feature switch, BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Diagnostics.Enabled. It is off unless the game opts in through its runtime config, typically in a Debug configuration: <RuntimeHostConfigurationOption Include="BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Diagnostics.Enabled" Value="true" Trim="true" />. It is always off where dynamic code is not supported, as under NativeAOT, and where it is off the trimmer removes the code it guards. A member called while it is off throws , except the two that generated code and engine glue call without asking first, RecordSource and , which then do nothing. An element tree belongs to the thread that ticks its host. A tool on another thread reaches it through (or , where every host ticks on one thread), and calls every member that reads or changes an element from the work it posts. The pipe a RoseMCP host loads a tap through is not here: a game that wants it references BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Diagnostics.Endpoint and starts it, so turning this switch on never by itself lets another process load code into the game.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Diagnostics.IFrameSource**: Engine glue that reads back the frame the game presented, so a diagnostics magnifier sees the scene behind the UI as well as the UI. Vysara never draws to the screen itself, so only the engine can supply this.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Diagnostics.PropertyValue**: One dependency property of an element as reads it.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Diagnostics.SourcePosition**: Where in a XAML file an element or a style setter was written.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Diagnostics.ValueLevel**: Where a dependency property's value came from: the levels of the precedence ladder, lowest first, so a greater level overrides a lesser one.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Documents.Typography**: WinUI's OpenType typography settings, as attached properties on the text they shape: <TextBlock Typography.NumeralAlignment="Tabular" />. Of WinUI's set, NumeralAlignment is here, set on a ; elsewhere it is VYSARA004, as Vysara has no inherited text properties yet. The text measures and draws with the features a setting names, so layout reserves the width the run draws at.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.DrawListBuffers**: One set of a surface's retained draw-list streams. A keeps two and fills them in turn, so the list it built last stays readable while it builds the next. names the composite that last filled the set; a bound to an older revision has had its contents overwritten.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.AtlasImage**: A glyph atlas page: the decoded RGBA8 MTSDF texels exposes. Vysara decodes the atlas PNG itself (no engine dependency); as a the page reaches the host through the slot table of every draw list whose glyph runs sample it. The texels are signed distances, so the page is , never sRGB-decoded, and is read as stored.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.DrawCommand**: One batched draw call in a draw list: a contiguous slice of the index stream drawn under a scissor rectangle with one texture bound. Blittable and sequentially laid out — the engine glue can reinterpret its memory as the equivalent engine draw command without copying.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.DrawListBuilder**: Builds a by hand, with the draw list the compositor uses, for a host's own overlays, demos and tests. It covers vector geometry from the , in a solid colour or a texture, and group layers, and nothing else: no gradients, rects or glyphs, which only 's walk emits. The full vector seam is the tessellator's own: , , and , from which a foreign draws paths its own way. Like a compositor's surface, a builder keeps two sets of buffers and fills them in turn: the list one returns stays readable through the next build, its streams throw once the build after that reuses them, and building lists of a steady size allocates nothing. The lists it builds sit outside texture residency: unless a compositor hands them to a as an , nothing reports the textures they sample in , and whoever draws them keeps and releases those textures itself.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.DrawListData**: One frame's flattened draw list — a variable-size vertex stream, its 16-bit index stream, and the batched draw commands that scissor + texture + index-range it. Backend-neutral (no graphics-API types), so the whole producer pipeline up to GPU upload is CPU-testable against . Rebuilt only when its source changes; an unchanged frame re-submits the same Revision. A list a produced is a view over buffers the compositor keeps and refills. It stays readable through the next composite of its surface, which fills a second set of buffers, and its streams (, , , , ) throw once a later composite refills its own set. Memory and spans taken from it share that lifetime but are not checked. The compositor also reuses the view objects, so a reference kept for four or more composites can be rebound to a newer list: read the surface's current list each frame rather than keeping one.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.DrawListId**: Identifies one draw list a surface's compositor produces each frame.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.EarClipper**: Triangulates a simple polygon with holes by ear clipping, after the algorithm of mapbox's earcut (ISC licence, © Mapbox): each hole is bridged into the outer ring at a vertex visible from its leftmost point, then ears (convex vertices whose triangle holds no other vertex) are clipped until one triangle is left. Degenerate input falls back to removing collinear points, curing local self-crossings and splitting along a valid diagonal, so it always terminates. The outer ring has a positive signed area (Σ x_i y_(i+1) - x_(i+1) y_i) and every hole a negative one. Nodes live in a retained pool, so triangulating polygons of a steady size allocates nothing.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.IVectorSink**: Receives the triangles a draws when emitted: the draw list's vector emitter, or a foreign compositor's own buffer. Implemented by a struct, it is called with no virtual dispatch and no allocation.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.OverlayVertex**: The vertex of a 2D overlay draw list — a pixel-space position, texture coordinate, premultiplied colour, and a float4 of per-vertex data the consuming technique defines. Blittable and sequentially laid out so it can be uploaded directly to a GPU vertex buffer.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.PremultipliedHdrColor**: A premultiplied RGBA16F colour — the wire format for the overlay vertex stream. Four Half components (8 bytes), blittable and sequentially laid out so the engine can upload it directly as GPU vertex data. Named PremultipliedHdrColor (not a bare four-Half vector) so the premultiplied-alpha contract is explicit in the type system; produced by .
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.StrokePrimitives**: The triangles a stroke is built from, each carrying the signed distances to the edges it antialiases. Shared by the tessellator, which builds a whole stroke, and by trimming at emit, which rebuilds the pieces cut at the trim points, so both draw identical geometry. Every piece reaches margin (half a pixel) past the true outline, so the antialiasing ramp is rasterized on the outside, and every distance is linear across its triangle. A triangle carries only the edges whose ramps it holds: a segment's body its two sides and any cap clip, a join or cap one outer edge per triangle (joins and caps are split on their bisectors so two nearly parallel edges never share a triangle, where the product of their ramps would darken the edge).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.SweepTessellator**: The GLU sweep-line tessellator (Eric Veach, SGI), ported from libtess2 under SGI Free Software License B: it resolves contours that cross themselves and each other into the planar arrangement they describe, keeps the regions a winding rule calls inside, and either triangulates them or returns their boundary as simple contours. Robust to degenerate input: coincident vertices merge, crossings get vertices, and zero-length edges and two-edge faces go. Planar only: the sweep plane is the input's own (s = x, t = y), with no normal to compute. The mesh, the event queue and the edge dictionary are pooled and their storage retained, so tessellating inputs of a steady size allocates nothing once warm.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.SweepTessellator.ActiveRegion**: The region between a pair of adjacent edges crossing the sweep line. Regions are kept in order in the edge dictionary; as the sweep line crosses each vertex, the affected regions are updated.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.SweepTessellator.DictNode**: A node of the edge dictionary: a sorted, circular, doubly-linked list with a key-less head.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.SweepTessellator.PriorityQueue**: The sweep's event queue: the vertices in VertLeq order, with insertion of new (intersection) vertices and deletion by handle. The initial vertices are sorted once into an array consumed from its end; vertices inserted later go into a heap. Extraction takes the smaller of the two minimums. Handles below zero name sorted-array slots, others heap handles. Its arrays are retained and grow by doubling.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.TessellatedPath**: A tessellated fill or stroke: triangles with three vertices each, never shared, whose corners carry the distances the vector prim antialiases with and their arc length. It is retained: tessellating into it again reuses its storage, so a path that keeps its size stops allocating, and drawing it, moved, recoloured or trimmed, allocates nothing. A stroke keeps its triangles in pieces ordered along its length: caps, segment bodies and joins. draws a trimmed stroke from those pieces: the ones inside the trim as they are, the two segments it cuts rebuilt to the trim points, and new caps there, so a draw-on animation never re-tessellates.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.TessellatedPath.Emitter`1**: Copies cached pieces to the sink, coalescing neighbours into one call, and rebuilds cut pieces into retained scratch.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.TessellatedPath.Piece**: One piece of a stroke: its run-coordinate range (a single point for a join or cap), its vertices, and for a body its segment, where along the segment it starts, and whether it carries its run's flat or square cap clip.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.TessellatedPath.Run**: One continuous stretch of stroke: a whole open figure, a whole closed figure (a loop), or one dash. Its range is in run coordinates, the figure's arc length, which runs past the figure's length when a dash crosses a closed figure's start.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.TessellatedPath.Segment**: One straight segment of a flattened figure: where it starts, its unit direction, its length, and the figure-local arc length at its start.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.TessellationScale**: The pixel scale a path is tessellated for, rounded to buckets half an octave wide, so a path that scales a little keeps its tessellation and one that zooms a lot gets a new one. Curves are flattened to within a quarter pixel at the top of the bucket of the largest scale the transform applies; antialiasing reaches half a pixel past each edge at the bottom of the bucket of the smallest, so it is never narrower than a pixel however the bucket rounds.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.Tessellator**: Turns a into antialiased triangles for the vector prim: a fill, or a stroke with WinUI's joins, caps and dashes. Curves are flattened to within a quarter pixel at the ; every edge the result shows carries a signed distance, so a renderer antialiases it exactly at any position, rotation or scale within the bucket. Public and dependency-free, so a foreign compositor can tessellate the composition's paths itself. It keeps scratch buffers between calls and writes into a retained , so re-tessellating paths of a steady size allocates nothing. One tessellator is not safe to use from two threads at once.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.Tessellator.Contour**: One contour to fill: a range of , its signed area, and what the nesting analysis decided about it.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.Tessellator.FigureRuns**: Where a figure's segments are in the output, and its length and offset along the whole geometry.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.Tessellator.FlatFigure**: One flattened figure: a range of , whether it is closed, whether it is filled, and whether it draws at all (a lone move does not).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.TextureAlphaMode**: How a 's colour channels relate to its alpha once its texels are decoded to linear light (). A host samples the texel (decoding and filtering as its texture format does) and, for a source, multiplies the sampled colour by the sampled alpha before using it, as every draw-list colour is premultiplied.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.TextureColorSpace**: How a 's RGB bytes encode light. A host binds an source through an sRGB texture format, so the hardware decodes each texel to linear light before filtering, and a one through a plain (UNORM) format, read as stored. Alpha is never encoded.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.TextureSource**: Texels a draw list samples through one of its texture slots: an image (), a glyph atlas page (), or the texel. A host uploads each source it meets in a list's and binds it by slot. A source is identified by reference, and moves when its texels change, so a host replaces an upload only when it is out of date. A source declares how to read its texels: says how the bytes decode to linear light (the texture format a host binds it through), and whether the decoded colour is premultiplied. Both are fixed for the source's life and belong to the slot, not to the commands that sample it, so every kind that samples a slot (an image quad, a textured vector triangle) reads it the same way.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.TransformStretch**: How much a 2D transform stretches lengths: the largest and smallest factors over all directions, the singular values of its linear part. A uniform scale s stretches every direction by s and a rotation by 1; a non-uniform scale or a skew stretches some directions more than others. Translation stretches nothing.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Drawing.VectorVertex**: One corner of a tessellated triangle: its position in the path's local space, the four signed distances a renderer turns into antialiased coverage, and its arc length along the stroke.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Extensions.Clipping**: Clipping to an element's own bounds, set in XAML as vysara:Clipping.ClipToBounds="True". WinUI has no such property: it clips with UIElement.Clip, a geometry. Here the element's composition node clips its subtree to the element's layout bounds. Controls that always clip (ScrollViewer, TextBox) do so whatever this says.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Extensions.GridResizeDirection**: Which tracks a resizes: worked out from its shape (wider than tall, rows), rows, or columns.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Extensions.GridSplitter**: A bar in a that resizes the tracks either side of it as it is dragged, as the Windows Community Toolkit's GridSplitter (WinUI has none, so it is <vysara:GridSplitter>). Placed in a row of its own (a thin Auto or pixel row) it resizes the rows above and below; in a column, the columns left and right. says which where its shape doesn't. As a primary drag starts both tracks become pixel tracks of the sizes they had, and they keep the sizes the drag leaves them, each no smaller than ; says so as it ends, and a drag whose capture is lost ends there. The bar paints the control's (a faint line unless set), with a grip while the pointer is over it or dragging it.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Extensions.HostImageSource**: An image whose texels the host supplies, named by : a render target, a video frame, anything the host draws itself. Vysara-only (WinUI has no such source) and code-only. It has a size, so it lays out and is placed by a brush's stretch like any image, but no texels: is empty, and a host binds its own texture for the tag to the source's slot (Kaldra: UIPainter.SetExternalTexture), reading it as and declare. A host that has nothing for the tag fails loud. The CPU rasterizer skips what samples it and counts the commands it skipped. The host owns the texture, so a released or disposed host image tells the host to stop binding it, not to destroy it. Its size is fixed: to show a resized target, make a new source with the same tag.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Extensions.InputPane**: Keeps content clear of an on-screen keyboard. Set vysara:InputPane.AvoidsKeyboard="True" on the element whose area the keyboard may cover, typically the page's main Border or Grid: while the keyboard is up, the element is arranged shorter by however much of it lies under the keyboard, so its * rows, a ScrollViewer or anything stretched inside it shrinks to the part still visible, and a text field at its bottom rises above the keyboard. Elements without it are left where they are, under the keyboard if that is where they are.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Extensions.SafeArea**: Keeps content clear of the parts of the screen that hide it: a phone's camera cutout, its rounded corners. Set vysara:SafeArea.Edges="All" (or Top, Left, …) on the element whose content must stay visible, typically the page's root: it is arranged inset by however much of it lies in the unsafe band along each edge it names, so a background can still run to the very edge of the screen while its content stays clear.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Extensions.SafeAreaEdges**: The edges of the surface an element keeps clear of where the screen hides content (see ).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Extensions.Scrolling**: Scrolling settings WinUI has no property for, set on a in XAML as vysara:Scrolling.WheelScrollAmount="64".
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Extensions.StrokeBrushMapping**: How a shape's stroke gradient is mapped, set in XAML as vysara:StrokeBrushMapping.Mode="AlongLength": with the gradient's offsets run along the stroke's untrimmed length, for a fade along a trail or a line coloured by progress. WinUI has no such mapping; it is set on the shape rather than the brush, so a brush shared by several elements never changes meaning with who shows it. It is exact: the stroke is cut where its colour stops being linear along it (at each stop), so a stop's colour lands exactly at its offset along the length. It suits a few stops; colouring each sample of a long line differently is a different feature, not provided. A solid or image stroke draws as usual.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Extensions.StrokeBrushMappingMode**: How a shape's Stroke gradient is laid over the stroke, set by .
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Extensions.StrokeTrim**: The part of a shape's stroke that is drawn, set in XAML as vysara:StrokeTrim.End="0.5": WinUI's CompositionGeometry.TrimStart, TrimEnd and TrimOffset lifted into markup, for draw-on reveals and segments that run round an outline. The values are fractions of the whole outline's length, all its figures in order: the stroke runs from Start to End, both moved along by Offset and wrapping past the end back to the start. Start and end are clamped to 0..1 and swapped when start is the larger; equal, they draw nothing. The trim applies where the shape is drawn: animating it, through a path such as (vysara:StrokeTrim.End), costs no layout and no tessellation, and allocates nothing. A trimmed stroke takes its start cap where it starts and its end cap where it ends. The fill is not trimmed.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Extensions.TextEffects**: An outline and a shadow on text, set in XAML on a as vysara:TextEffects.OutlineThickness="0.08" vysara:TextEffects.OutlineBrush="Black", and ShadowOffset, ShadowSoftness and ShadowBrush. WinUI has neither for text. Both are drawn in the text's own draw from the font atlas's true-distance channel, and sized in EM, so they scale with the font size. The outline is the glyphs grown by its thickness. The shadow is the glyphs moved by its offset, their edge fading across its softness, centred on the moved edge; it is cast by the glyphs, not their outline. Every glyph's shadow lies under every glyph's outline, and every outline under every glyph, so an opaque effect is exact: no glyph's effect covers a neighbouring glyph. A translucent effect blends twice where neighbouring glyphs' effects overlap (outlines meet between letters, soft halos run into each other), a gap; a soft translucent shadow needs a drop shadow on the element's whole layer instead. The outline lies under the whole glyph rather than round it, so a translucent shows it through. Fading the element with Opacity fades the text and its effects as one. The atlas holds distances / 2 past each edge, so an outline can be at most that thick and a shadow at most soft, as it fades half its softness past the edge; at a small size, less, since the edge's own ramp takes some of the field. An effect its font's field cannot hold at the size it is drawn is drawn clamped to what it can, whatever the order the text, its font and its root were put together in, and the text's visual says so in . A negative or non-finite size throws whenever it is set, as does an animation that names one (its start and end, its keyframes) as it begins. The effects take a colour or a linear gradient, measured over the text's layout box (moved with the shadow, for the shadow); an image brush throws when set. Animating a size, the offset or a brush costs no layout and no shaping, and allocates nothing. Set on anything but a they are VYSARA004, as Vysara has no inherited text properties yet.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Extensions.Virtualization**: Settings for Vysara's , set in XAML as <VirtualizingStackPanel vysara:Virtualization.RowHeight="32" /> inside an ItemsPanelTemplate. WinUI's virtualizing panels measure their items; Vysara's assumes one uniform row height, so the visible window is arithmetic from the scroll offset.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.FieldAccessor`2**: The field of that holds a field-backed property's value (), by reference.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.FocusManager**: Per-host focus state machine. Tracks the focused element, raises the four focus routed events (GettingFocus/LosingFocus tunnel, GotFocus/LostFocus bubble), and drives Tab/Shift-Tab navigation across a set of s respecting , and . Tab order runs across all the views as one sequence: no subtree keeps focus within itself, and is not read. Up, down, left and right (a gamepad's d-pad, ) move focus by position instead, to the nearest tab stop that way within the focused element's view, or its and the like; a control shows how it holds focus in its template's FocusStates.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.FocusState**: How focus was most recently acquired on an element (WinUI-compatible).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.FontAtlas**: A baked MTSDF font atlas: the decoded atlas page plus per-glyph layout, loaded from the pair an MSDF generator emits — a PNG page (RGBA8 MTSDF) and a JSON layout. The page is decoded linear/UNORM, no mips: MTSDF texels are signed distances, never sRGB colour. Plane bounds are EM units in a y-down, baseline-at-origin frame.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.FontFeature**: One OpenType feature setting for a shaper: a four-letter such as tnum (packed big-endian, as the font's tables store it) and its : 1 turns a feature on and 0 off; a feature that picks one of several alternates takes the alternate's index.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.FontFeatureSet**: The OpenType feature settings a run of text is shaped with, immutable and compared by value. An takes one for both measuring and laying out a run, so the width layout reserves is the width the run draws at. Each tag appears once: a later setting of the same tag replaces an earlier one. The settings are kept in tag order, so two sets that set the same tags to the same values are equal however they were written. Sets are cheap to share; the common ones are kept here so an element switching between them allocates nothing.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.FontNumeralAlignment**: How the widths of digits are aligned, set by : WinUI's FontNumeralAlignment.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.FrameworkElement**: Adds the WinUI framework-level layout inputs on top of : explicit / (NaN = Auto), / (and the height pair), , and alignment. It implements the WinUI MeasureCore/ArrangeCore wrapper — deflate by margin, clamp to min/max/explicit, call the element's MeasureOverride/ArrangeOverride, reinflate — so every control only writes its intrinsic sizing. The layout inputs are dependency properties, as in WinUI, so a sets them and a storyboard animates the sizes. Layout reads them on every pass, so they are field-backed, as WinUI's core keeps them: each one's value is in a field here, which measure and arrange read, and an element whose layout only code or markup set holds nothing for them in the property store.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Generated.TemplateValues**: What a generated ControlTemplate factory calls to set a value on a part of the template, as WinUI sets every value a template gives its parts: at the templated-parent level, below the part's local value. So a value the app sets on a part wins over the template's, ClearValue on a part goes back to the template's value rather than dropping it, and a diagnostics tool reports the value as the template's. In a namespace markup doesn't map, since it is for generated code only.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Glyph**: One baked glyph from a . Plane bounds are EM units in a y-down, baseline-at-origin frame (the on-screen quad, scaled by the font px size); the UV rect addresses the glyph's MTSDF cell in the atlas page (0..1, v=0 at the top — the atlas is baked with yOrigin: top).
