Whitespace glyphs set false and carry only an . is the source Unicode code point (−1 for a glyph with none, e.g. a ligature in a glyph-id-keyed atlas). is the font glyph index (−1 in a codepoint-keyed atlas that does not record ids) — the key a shaper such as HarfBuzz addresses glyphs by.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.GlyphLayer**: What a glyph run's quads draw (): the glyphs, or one of the effects drawn from the atlas's true-distance channel under them.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.GradientLine**: Where a linear gradient lies in the local space of what it paints: measures a point along it, 0 at the start and 1 at the end, constant across it. A gradient whose start and end coincide is , and paints its last stop's colour everywhere.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.GradientSplitter**: Paints convex polygons with a linear gradient exactly, with no ramp texture: the polygon is cut into bands wherever the gradient's colour stops being linear along it (each stop, each repeat of a wrapping gradient, and each piece of an sRGB-interpolated interval), and every corner of every band gets the gradient's colour at that point. Within a band the colour is linear in position, which is exactly what interpolating vertex colours across a triangle produces, so a GPU and the CPU rasterizer draw the gradient itself, colours above paper white included. Each corner keeps its uv, interpolated where a cut crosses an edge, so a rectangle's bands keep their part of its 0..1 uv (the rounded-rectangle and border shading reads it, with the whole rectangle's size, to find its edges) and a glyph's pieces keep their part of its atlas cell. A vector triangle's pieces keep their part of its edge distances the same way, which are linear across it, so the pieces antialias exactly as the whole triangle would. Allocation-free: the pieces are built on the stack.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.GridLength**: A Grid row/column track length — fixed pixels, Auto (max child desired), or a * weight of the leftover space (WinUI GridLength). Default is 1*, matching WinUI.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.GridUnitType**: How a is interpreted: a fixed DIP size, content-sized, or a proportional star.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.HdrColor**: An authoring colour — float RGBA where 0..1 is SDR / paper-white range and a component >1 is above paper white (opt-in HDR). Named HdrColor (not Color) for explicitness and to dodge the clash. Folded to a by the compositor; the paper-white reference scale is applied in the shader.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.HorizontalAlignment**: WinUI alignment within a layout slot's horizontal axis. fills the slot.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.HotReload**: XAML Hot Reload support. A generated view registers itself here in InitializeComponent() and each registers itself on construction. When the runtime applies a metadata delta (an edited .xaml re-runs the source generator under dotnet watch), the records the changed types; the next drains them and rebuilds the affected views on the UI thread — never on the hot-reload agent's thread. A view rebuilds wherever it sits in a live host's tree, nested in another view as much as hosted as a , and its code-behind hears of it through the generated partial void OnComponentRebuilt(). Bookkeeping is gated on , which defaults to and is always false where dynamic code is not supported: under NativeAOT it reads as a constant false, so the trimmer removes the code it guards, preserving the reflection-free runtime. Tests force it on.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.HotReloadHandler**: The [MetadataUpdateHandler] target (registered as an assembly attribute in ). The runtime invokes these after applying a metadata delta; they hand the changed types to , which defers the actual view rebuild to the next .
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.IGlyphSource**: The font read-surface a text shaper (and any glyph consumer) needs, independent of how glyphs are imaged: code-point and glyph-id lookups returning the drawable cell, advances, and EM line metrics. is the MTSDF implementation; a different imagery backend (e.g. a bitmap atlas) can implement the same interface, so the shaping backend () and the imagery backend swap independently — a shaper is written against this interface, never a concrete atlas. Render-technique specifics (e.g. an MTSDF distance range) are deliberately kept off this interface.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.IInheritedMember`1**: One owner's dependency property for an .
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.ISubPropertyListener**: Something that shows a shared sub-property object (a brush, a transform, a gradient stop, a geometry) and is told when that object changes, so it can bring what it draws up to date without re-reading anything else. An element listens to the brushes, transform and clip geometry it shows while it is in a live tree; a brush listens to its gradient stops, a transform group to its children, and a geometry to its figures, segments and points.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.ITextShaper**: Turns a run of text into positioned glyphs against an — it is written against the source interface, never a concrete atlas, so the shaping backend and the imagery backend stay independent. The default is advance-based, one glyph per code point (no kerning or ligatures); a real shaper (e.g. HarfBuzz) applies the font's GSUB/GPOS to produce ligatures, contextual forms, and kerning, resolving the glyph ids it emits back through the source. A owns the active shaper, so swapping it changes layout everywhere (measure, the compositor's glyph runs, caret math) at once. Both calls take the run's OpenType ( for the defaults). A shaper applies the features it can and ignores the rest; measuring and laying out with the same set give the same width.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.IValueConverter**: Converts a value between binding source and target types. Implement this for converter= attributes in XAML bindings; pass a singleton instance via {StaticResource key}.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.InheritedProperty`1**: A property whose value flows down the element tree, as WinUI's text properties do: each type that holds it registers a dependency property of its own (Control.FontSize, ContentPresenter.FontSize, TextBlock.FontSize), and an element's value of it becomes the Inherited value of the nearest elements below that hold one, through any between that don't (a Border, a Panel). A value set on an element locally, by a style or by an animation outranks the one it inherits, and is what its own descendants inherit in turn. The value is pushed, not looked up: when an element's value changes, the elements below that take it are told at once, and an element joining a parent takes the value the parent passes down (and gives it up on leaving), so reading one never walks the tree and a steady frame does no inheritance work. The members share a default, so an element below nothing that holds a value reads the same as one below an element that holds only the default.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Input.FocusNavigationDirection**: Direction of programmatic or keyboard-driven focus movement.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Input.KeyInput**: One device-neutral keyboard event the host queues into between frames. The host (Sandbox/Silk.NET) translates raw platform key events into this, keeping windowing types out of Vysara.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Input.ModifierKeys**: Modifier keys held at the time of a keyboard or pointer event.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Input.PointerButtons**: The set of pointer buttons currently held.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Input.PointerDeviceType**: The kind of device that produced a — WinUI-shaped and device-neutral so no host (Silk.NET) type leaks into Vysara. Only is currently driven; pen and touch use the same struct.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Input.PointerInput**: One device-neutral pointer event the host queues into a between frames. WinUI-shaped so mouse, pen and touch share one struct; the host (Sandbox/Silk.NET) translates raw input into this, keeping graphics/windowing types out of Vysara. is in surface pixels (the same space as the composited DrawListData / the framebuffer); the host hit-tests and routes it in .
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Input.PointerUpdateKind**: What changed in a — the WinUI PointerUpdateKind. A plain move carries ; a button edge carries the specific pressed/released kind that the input pipeline turns into PointerPressed/PointerReleased routed events (and, on a matching pair, a synthesized Click).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Input.VirtualKey**: Virtual key codes (WinUI-compatible subset). Values match Windows virtual-key codes so host adapters can cast directly from platform key enumerations.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.InputManager**: Per-host pointer routing: hit-tests each queued over the host's interactive overlay views, raises tunnel-then-bubble pointer routed events, tracks the "over" chain (so enter/exit fire per element), implicitly captures on press so a press→release pair routes to the same target (the basis for Button.Click), and supports explicit drag capture via /. Persistent host state; headless (no engine/backend).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.InvalidationFlags**: Which layout/render stages a property change invalidates — ORed up the tree on a resolved-value change A pure-render change (a brush colour) sets only ; a sizing change sets .
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.ListenerList**: The s a shared sub-property object tells when it changes. A listener that shows the object twice (an element using one brush for its background and its border) is added, told and removed once per use. Telling them allocates nothing.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Markup.IPathMarkupSink**: What reports as it reads WinUI path markup: the fill rule, then each figure as a start point and drawing commands, all in absolute coordinates. Relative commands, H/V and the smooth S/T forms arrive already resolved to the absolute line and curve they draw.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Markup.PathMarkup**: WinUI's path markup, the move-and-draw command syntax of Path.Data: an optional fill rule (F0 even-odd, F1 nonzero), then figures, each a move (M) followed by lines (L, H, V), cubic Béziers (C, smooth S), quadratic Béziers (Q, smooth T), elliptical arcs (A) and an optional close (Z). A lowercase command is relative to the current point, and a command's parameters may repeat to draw several of it (after M, further points are lines). Numbers are separated by commas and/or whitespace and must be finite; arc flags are 0 or 1. The grammar is held strictly: markup must start with a move, a close is followed by a move or the end, and anything else is an error naming its character position. This file is compiled into both the runtime and the netstandard2.0 XAML generator, so markup in XAML is checked at compile time by the parser the runtime uses.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Markup.XamlValueSyntax**: The text forms XAML values take: colours (#RRGGBB, #AARRGGBB, or one of WinUI's named colours), lists of numbers separated by commas or whitespace (points, vectors, thicknesses), grid lengths, durations and repeat behaviours. This file is compiled into both the runtime and the netstandard2.0 XAML generator, which links it as source, so a value the generator accepts at compile time parses the same way at runtime. It uses only APIs both targets have.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Markup.XamlValueSyntax.GridLengthForm**: The three forms a grid length takes.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.AlignmentX**: Where a tile brush places its content across the area painted, as WinUI's AlignmentX.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.AlignmentY**: Where a tile brush places its content down the area painted, as WinUI's AlignmentY.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.ArcSegment**: An elliptical arc to , as WinUI's ArcSegment: part of an ellipse with radii , rotated by degrees. Of the four arcs such an ellipse can draw between the two points, and pick one. Radii too small to reach the end grow, keeping their ratio, until they just do.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.BezierSegment**: A cubic Bézier curve to , bent by the control points and , as WinUI's BezierSegment.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.Brush**: What paints an element's area, text or border, as WinUI's Brush: a , a or an . A brush is shareable, as in WinUI: put one in a ResourceDictionary and give it to many elements. Each brush keeps one retained , which every element showing it paints with, and a change to the brush updates that paint in place and marks those elements' visuals dirty, with no layout and no allocation. An element registers with a brush while it is in a live tree and unregisters when it leaves, so a long-lived brush does not keep removed elements, or the trees a hot-reload rebuild replaced, alive. Because the brush is shared, so are its animations: a storyboard that animates a shared brush, such as (Border.Background).(SolidColorBrush.Color) on a border whose background is a resource, recolours every element showing that brush, as it does in WinUI. Give an element its own brush to animate it alone. Like any dependency object, a brush belongs to the UI thread of the elements that show it. The brushes of Vysara's built-in control look are the exception: they are sealed, so they are shared by every control on every thread, keep no listeners, and throw if anything tries to change them.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.BrushMappingMode**: What a gradient brush's points are measured in, as WinUI's BrushMappingMode.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.ColorInterpolationMode**: The space a gradient's colours interpolate in, as WinUI's ColorInterpolationMode.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.CompositeTransform**: Scale, skew, rotation and translation in one, as WinUI's CompositeTransform, applied in that order: scale, skew and rotation about (, ), then the translation. Angles are in degrees. The usual target of a storyboard that moves an element: (UIElement.RenderTransform).(CompositeTransform.TranslateX).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.CompositionValues**: The element layer's values as the composition layer takes them, where an element or a brush pushes them into its retained composition objects. The composition layer has enums of its own, so its contract names no element-layer type: , and mirror WinUI's Microsoft.UI.Composition ones, and , and , which have no counterpart there, take their members from the XAML enums. A value outside its enum maps to the value the composition object starts with.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.DoubleCollection**: An ordered list of numbers, as WinUI's DoubleCollection: a shape's dash pattern, for one. Every change is reported to the element using it. In XAML it is written as numbers separated by commas or spaces, StrokeDashArray="2 1".
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.EllipseGeometry**: An axis-aligned ellipse around , as WinUI's EllipseGeometry. A zero radius draws nothing.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.FillRule**: How a geometry whose figures overlap or cross themselves decides what is inside, as WinUI's FillRule.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.GeneralTransform**: Maps points and rects from one coordinate space to another, as WinUI's GeneralTransform: the base of every , and what returns. A transform that cannot map a point (one into an element scaled to nothing) reports it through .
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.Geometry**: A 2D shape, as WinUI's Geometry: what a Path draws and what clips to. Every property of every part is a dependency property, so geometries are stylable and their numbers animatable. A change anywhere in a geometry, down to one point of a segment, is reported to its listeners: the group or element using it. An element registers while it is in a live tree and unregisters when it leaves, so a geometry kept in a resource dictionary never keeps removed elements alive. Each geometry keeps its , the neutral path the compositor and the tessellator read, and rebuilds it in place after a change, reusing its storage. A geometry is drawn in the local space of the element that draws it, through its if it has one. The transform is applied where the geometry is used rather than to its path, so moving it does not rebuild the path.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.GeometryCollection**: A geometry group's children, as WinUI's GeometryCollection. A geometry may be in several collections, and in one more than once.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.GeometryGroup**: Several geometries drawn as one, as WinUI's GeometryGroup: their figures together, each through its own , filled by the group's own (the children's fill rules are not used), so overlapping children cut holes under and merge under . The group's own transform applies on top, where the group is used.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.GradientBrush**: The stops and modes a gradient brush shares, as WinUI's GradientBrush; places them along a line. The stops are the brush's XAML content: <LinearGradientBrush><GradientStop Color="Red" Offset="0"/>…</LinearGradientBrush> Colours interpolate as premultiplied values. is drawn exactly, colours above paper white included, by splitting what is painted where the stops fall: there is no ramp texture to clamp or quantize them. The default, , cuts each stop interval into eight pieces, exact at their ends and within the error documents between them, and a stop above 1 in it throws when the brush is drawn.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.GradientSpreadMethod**: What a gradient paints before its start and past its end, as WinUI's GradientSpreadMethod.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.GradientStop**: One colour of a , at along it, as WinUI's GradientStop. Both are animatable; a change reaches every brush holding the stop, and from there every element showing the brush, with no layout and no allocation. Name a stop with x:Name to target it from a storyboard.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.GradientStopCollection**: The stops of one , as WinUI's GradientStopCollection, in any order: the brush orders them by offset. Adding, removing or replacing a stop, or changing one, updates the brush's paint in place. A stop may sit in more than one brush's collection, and a change to it reaches each.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.ImageBrush**: Paints an image, as WinUI's ImageBrush: scaled into the area painted by and placed by and , cut at the area's edges. It paints a Panel's or Border's background, rounded or not, a Border's border, and a shape's fill or stroke; text is not supported yet, and throws when drawn.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.ImageSource**: An image an or an draws, as WinUI's ImageSource: a (decoded texels that never change), a (texels the app rewrites), or a (texels the host supplies). Each declares its and , so straight-alpha and sRGB images blend correctly. Unlike WinUI's, an image source is itself the neutral a draw list's slot holds: it has no dependency properties of its own, so it is not a DependencyObject, and the composition layer needs no second object for it. Lifetime. A host keeps an image's texture while any of its surfaces draws the image, and is told to release it once none does (), including an image a hot-reload rebuild left behind. (Vysara-only, as WinUI's image sources are not disposable) lets it go without waiting for nothing to draw it: each host that draws the image redraws without it at its next render and releases its texture then. An image keeps no reference to the hosts that draw it, so a long-lived one keeps none of them alive.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.Imaging.BitmapSource**: An image of decoded RGBA8 texels, as WinUI's BitmapSource. One made by or never changes; is the one whose texels the app rewrites. Vysara stays GPU-free: the texels are neutral bytes (decoded with StbImageSharp, the decoder uses), and reach the host through the slot table of every draw list that draws the image. The factories are Vysara's (WinUI loads a bitmap from a stream or a URI). By default the texels are what an image file holds: sRGB-encoded colour with straight alpha.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.Imaging.WriteableBitmap**: An image whose texels the app writes, as WinUI's WriteableBitmap: change , then call to show the change. moves the image's , so every surface drawing it moves its on its next frame, with no layout and no recomposite, and a host brings its texture up to date. A host that can update a texture in place writes the new texels into the one it has, ordered after the frames still sampling it (Kaldra's painter does, through IEngine.UpdateTexture); one that cannot uploads them as a new texture and releases the old one once the frames in flight are done with it. Nothing on Vysara's side allocates, so a bitmap can be rewritten every frame; whether the host's side does is the host's. Unlike WinUI's, whose buffer is BGRA8 with premultiplied alpha, the buffer is RGBA8, like every , and is by default sRGB-encoded colour with straight alpha; the constructor that takes an alpha mode and a colour space is Vysara's.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.LineGeometry**: A straight line from to , as WinUI's LineGeometry. It encloses nothing, so it only draws when stroked.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.LineSegment**: A straight line to , as WinUI's LineSegment.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.LinearGradientBrush**: Paints a gradient along the line from to , as WinUI's LinearGradientBrush: the colour is constant across the line, and the stops' offsets measure along it. The default line runs from the top left (0,0) to the bottom right (1,1) of the area painted. With that area is the element's: a border's rectangle, or a text block's layout box for its text. If the start and end coincide, the last stop's colour fills the area.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.MatrixTransform**: An arbitrary affine transform given as a matrix, as WinUI's MatrixTransform. Vysara's matrix is (single precision, row vectors: M11 M12 / M21 M22 / M31 M32 as WinUI's M11 M12 / M21 M22 / OffsetX OffsetY); in XAML it is six numbers in that order. Not animatable, as a matrix has no interpolation.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.PathFigure**: One connected outline of a , as WinUI's PathFigure: it starts at and runs through its in order. A figure belongs to one geometry's at a time.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.PathFigureCollection**: A path geometry's figures, as WinUI's PathFigureCollection. A figure belongs to one collection at a time: adding one that another collection holds throws, as WinUI does.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.PathGeometry**: A geometry of any shape, as WinUI's PathGeometry: of lines, Béziers and arcs, filled by . In XAML it is written as figure elements, or as path markup where a property takes a (Data="M 0,0 L 10,0 10,10 Z"), which also reads.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.PathMarkupBuilder**: Builds a from parsed path markup: one figure per move, and one segment per run of the same command, so L 1,1 2,2 3,3 becomes a single and one line stays a . Arcs are one each, as they cannot share one.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.PathSegment**: One piece of a 's outline, drawn from where the piece before it ended, as WinUI's PathSegment. A segment belongs to one figure's at a time.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.PathSegmentCollection**: A figure's segments, in drawing order, as WinUI's PathSegmentCollection. A segment belongs to one collection at a time: adding one that another collection holds throws, as WinUI does.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.PenLineCap**: The shape at the end of a stroke or of one of its dashes, as WinUI's PenLineCap.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.PenLineJoin**: How a stroke turns a corner, as WinUI's PenLineJoin.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.PointCollection**: An ordered list of points, as WinUI's PointCollection: the vertices of a poly segment (and of a polyline or polygon). Every change is reported to the geometry or element using it. In XAML it is written as pairs of numbers, Points="0,0 10,10 20,0".
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.PolyBezierSegment**: Cubic Bézier curves, one per three of (two control points and an end point), as WinUI's PolyBezierSegment. Points left over after the last whole three draw nothing.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.PolyLineSegment**: Straight lines through each of in turn, as WinUI's PolyLineSegment.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.PolyQuadraticBezierSegment**: Quadratic Bézier curves, one per two of (a control point and an end point), as WinUI's PolyQuadraticBezierSegment. A point left over after the last whole pair draws nothing.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.QuadraticBezierSegment**: A quadratic Bézier curve to , bent by the control point , as WinUI's QuadraticBezierSegment.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.RectangleGeometry**: An axis-aligned rectangle, as WinUI's RectangleGeometry: what takes. In XAML, Rect="x,y,width,height".
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.RotateTransform**: Rotates by degrees, clockwise on screen, about (, ), as WinUI's RotateTransform.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.ScaleTransform**: Scales by and about (, ), as WinUI's ScaleTransform.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.SkewTransform**: Skews about (, ), as WinUI's SkewTransform: x moves by y·tan() and y by x·tan(), angles in degrees.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.SolidColorBrush**: Paints one colour, as WinUI's SolidColorBrush. In XAML a colour string (Background="#22252E", Background="CornflowerBlue") makes one.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.SweepDirection**: The direction an elliptical arc is drawn in, as WinUI's SweepDirection. Directions are as seen on screen, where y grows downward.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.TileBrush**: A brush that paints content scaled into the area painted, as WinUI's TileBrush: the base of .
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.Transform**: A 2D affine transform, as WinUI's Transform: an element's , or a child of a . Its properties are dependency properties, so a storyboard animates them through paths such as (UIElement.RenderTransform).(CompositeTransform.TranslateX). A change moves every element showing the transform on the visual path, with no layout. Like a brush, a transform may be shared: an element registers with it while it is in a live tree.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.TransformCollection**: The children of a , as WinUI's TransformCollection. Adding, removing or replacing a child, or changing one, moves every element showing the group.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.TransformGroup**: Transforms applied one after another, in the order lists them, as WinUI's TransformGroup. A change to any child, or to the list, moves every element showing the group.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.TranslateTransform**: Moves by (, ) DIPs, as WinUI's TranslateTransform.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Media.VisualTreeHelper**: The visual tree walked from outside it, as WinUI's VisualTreeHelper: an element's parent, and its children in the order they are drawn. A template's parts are children of the control they make up.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Orientation**: The axis a stacks along.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Point**: A point in DIPs (layout-space). Distinct from only for readability at call sites.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.PropertyMetadata`2**: The typed metadata for a : default value, a typed change callback (old, new — no boxing on the typed path), an optional coerce, what it invalidates, and how it interpolates when animated. Callbacks are static by convention (captured once at registration — no per-instance delegate, no reflection).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Rect**: An axis-aligned rectangle in pixels — neutral geometry used for layout, hit-testing, clip rects, and draw commands. Stored as origin + size so a zero-size rect is unambiguous; Right/Bottom are derived.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.ResourceDictionary**: A keyed resource store used by and resolved at compile time by the XAML source generator for {StaticResource key} references. Runtime lookup walks in reverse-index order (later entries take priority).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.RetainedBuffer`1**: A growable array that keeps its storage when cleared: the backing store of a stream rebuilt every frame. It grows by doubling, so a stream that settles at a steady size stops allocating, and its contents are handed out as over the live array rather than copied.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.RoutedEvents.CharacterReceivedRoutedEventArgs**: Event args for .
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.RoutedEvents.GettingFocusEventArgs**: Event args for and (both tunnel). Handlers may set to prevent the focus transfer from completing.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.RoutedEvents.KeyRoutedEventArgs**: Event args for , , and their Preview counterparts.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.RoutedEvents.PointerPoint**: A snapshot of a pointer at the moment of a routed pointer event — the WinUI PointerPoint, trimmed to what pointer routing needs. On , is in surface pixels; gives it in an element's DIPs.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.RoutedEvents.PointerRoutedEventArgs**: Payload for the pointer routed events: the and the originating . Pooled by the input pipeline.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.RoutedEvents.RoutedEvent**: A routed-event identity: a dense assigned at registration, a diagnostic , and the strategy. Registered once in a static field initializer (deterministic, AOT-safe — no assembly scanning), the same self-registration shape as . The dense id keys the per-element handler store with no string lookup.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.RoutedEvents.RoutedEventArgs**: The base routed-event payload. is the element the event was raised on; is the current element as the route advances; short-circuits the remaining route (a handler that registered handledEventsToo still runs). Mutable + reusable so the input pipeline can pool one instance per dispatch (honouring the "0 GC in the render loop" rule).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.RoutedEvents.RoutedEventHandler**: The single routed-event delegate shape — typed, so invocation is a direct call with no MethodInfo.Invoke and no argument boxing (the NAOT requirement). The generator wires handlers to it (btn.Click += this.OnClick), signature-checked at generate time.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.RoutedEvents.RoutingStrategy**: How a travels the element tree. goes root→target (WinUI Preview*), target→root, fires only on the target.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Setter**: A single property assignment within a . Writes the Style rung of the DP precedence ladder, so Local values and animations still win over a Style-sourced value.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.ShapedGlyph**: One positioned glyph produced by an : the atlas to draw, the pen position and per-glyph offsets it sits at (all in EM units, baseline at the origin — the layout scales them by the on-screen font px size), and the source-text (the index of the character it derives from, for caret / hit-test mapping). Whitespace and other zero-geometry glyphs are omitted from a shaped run.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.ShapedGlyphRun**: A shaped: its positioned glyphs in EM, line by line, and each line's width, kept on the content as the work derived from it () and refilled in place. It records what it was shaped from, the text, font, features and shaper, so a content change that leaves those alone (a resize, a new brush, a new alignment) keeps it.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.ShapedLine**: One line of a : glyphs from , its advance width in EM, and the width alignment places, in EM: the advance less any whitespace at the line's end.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Shapes.Ellipse**: An ellipse, as WinUI's Ellipse: the one inscribed in the space it is given, its by default (a circle with ), its stroke inside that space. It asks only for room for its pen, so give it a size or a stretching layout slot.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Shapes.Line**: A straight line from (, ) to (, ), as WinUI's Line. It encloses nothing, so it is only stroked.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Shapes.Path**: Draws a , as WinUI's Path: , through its . In XAML Data is often path markup, Data="M 0,0 L 10,10 20,0 Z". A change anywhere in the geometry, down to one point, applies in place, as does one to its transform.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Shapes.PointOutline**: The outline of a or a : one figure through its points, closed for a polygon, rebuilt in place on the first read after the points or the fill rule change, so moving the points allocates nothing. It is keyed by the collection's own version, so a change made while the shape was not listening (before it joined a live tree) is still seen.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Shapes.Polygon**: A closed outline through in turn, as WinUI's Polygon: the last point joins the first. In XAML, Points="0,0 10,5 20,0". A change to the points applies in place; from code, replaces them all with one change and no allocation.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Shapes.Polyline**: Straight lines through in turn, as WinUI's Polyline: an open outline, filled as if it were closed. In XAML, Points="0,0 10,5 20,0". A change to the points applies in place; from code, replaces them all with one change and no allocation.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Shapes.Rectangle**: A rectangle, its corners optionally rounded, as WinUI's Rectangle. It is sized by the space it is given rather than by an outline of its own: its is by default, and its stroke lies inside that space. It asks only for room for its pen, so give it a size or a stretching layout slot.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Shapes.Shape**: The base of the vector shapes, as WinUI's Shape: an outline filled by and stroked by with WinUI's stroke set (thickness, dashes, joins, miter limit and caps), sized by . Every property is a dependency property, so a shape is stylable and its numbers and colours animatable. A shape draws through one retained , which it updates in place when a property changes and never per frame. The tessellation is cached there, so moving, fading or recolouring a shape (its render transform, its opacity, its brushes' colours) costs no layout and no tessellation. While it is in a live tree a shape listens to its brushes, its dash array and its outline's geometry or points, as any element listens to its brushes. Layout. With the outline is drawn in the shape's own coordinates, and the shape asks for the space from its origin to the outline's far edges, the pen included when there is a stroke. Otherwise the outline is scaled into the space the shape is given, half the pen kept inside each edge: in each direction on its own, by the smaller scale and by the larger, keeping its proportions. An outline that does not fill the space is centred in it. The pen is never scaled. A and an are sized by the space itself instead. Hit-testing follows what is drawn: a point hits inside the fill when is set, and on the stroke, within half its thickness of the outline along the dashes, caps and joins it draws, when is. A shape with neither is not hit.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.SimpleTextShaper**: The default : advance-based, left-to-right, one glyph per code point — no kerning, ligatures, or contextual forms. Each glyph's cluster is its character index. This is the glyph layout a font with no installed shaper uses. Of the OpenType features it applies one, tnum, the one it can without the font's tables: every ASCII digit advances by the widest digit's advance, centred in it, so columns of numbers line up. Others, pnum included, leave the font's own advances, so a font whose digits are tabular by design stays tabular here.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Size**: A width/height pair in device-independent pixels (DIPs). Either component may be during measure (an unconstrained axis). Mirrors WinUI's Size.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Stretch**: How an scales its source into its layout bounds (WinUI Stretch).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Style**: An ordered collection of s applied to a via the Style rung of the DP precedence ladder. forms a chain: base setters apply first so derived setters override them. When replaced, the previous style's setters are cleared before the new style is applied.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.SurfaceTextures**: The sources one surface's current draw list holds through a host's , updated when the list's slot table may have changed.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.TabFocusNavigation**: Controls how Tab navigation behaves within a subtree (WinUI-compatible).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.TextAlignment**: How each line of text sits across the width its text block is arranged at, set by : WinUI's TextAlignment, with its values. Vysara lays text out left to right only, so is and is , the values they share in WinUI. Whitespace at the end of a line hangs past where the line is placed, so a trailing space does not move right-aligned or centred text.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.TextFit**: How a run's lines are fitted to a width: broken at spaces to keep inside it, cut short with an ellipsis, or neither (the default, in which the width means nothing).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.TextLines**: Where a text's lines break: at Unicode's mandatory breaks (UAX #14's BK, CR, LF and NL classes), so a line ends at a line feed, a carriage return (with the line feed after it, if any, as one break), a vertical tab, a form feed, a next line, a line separator or a paragraph separator. Text with none is one line; a break at the end leaves an empty line after it.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.TextTrimming**: What becomes of a line still wider than its text block after any wrapping, set by : WinUI's TextTrimming, with the values Vysara draws.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.TextWrapping**: Whether a text block's lines break where they would run past its width, set by : WinUI's TextWrapping. A line breaks after the last space that keeps it inside the width; a word wider than the width alone stays whole, on a line of its own, past it (unless cuts it).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.TextureResidency**: The texture sources a 's surfaces draw, counted across them, and those its last render let go of. A source is held exactly while the current draw list of one of the host's surfaces names it in its slot table, so one reported in is named by no list the host is about to draw. A disposed source is found at the start of the next render, and the surfaces that drew it are redrawn without it in that render, which therefore releases it. is never counted or reported: a host keeps it for its whole life. Sources keep no reference to the hosts that hold them, so a long-lived source (the default font atlas, a cached image) never keeps a host or its trees alive, and disposing a source on another thread touches no host state.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Thickness**: Per-edge spacing in DIPs — used for Margin, Padding, and border thickness (WinUI Thickness).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.ToolTipPresenter**: A host's tooltips (): ticked once a frame after input, it finds the element with a tooltip nearest the pointer's leaf, counts how long the pointer has rested on it, and shows the tooltip in that element's root's overlay layer, placed against it. One shows at a time. A press, a wheel turn or a key hides it, and it stays hidden until the pointer moves to another element. A steady frame allocates nothing; showing one makes its panel.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.TypedEventHandler`2**: A handler of an event that passes its sender as its own type, as WinUI's TypedEventHandler (Expander.Expanding, NumberBox.ValueChanged, InfoBar.Closed).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.UIDrawList**: A surface's retained draw-list builder — the analog of ImGui's ImDrawList. Bakes the composed transform into vertex positions and merges consecutive primitives that share (kind, texture slot, clip) into one indexed draw command (atlas-everything + state-run batching). It keeps two sets and fills them in turn, so the list it built last stays readable (for damage, and for a host still holding it) while the next one builds, and a surface stops allocating once both sets have grown to its size. Each list is handed out through a ring of reused views. Indices are 16-bit and relative to a window of at most vertices, which each command names by its . When a primitive would not fit in the current window, the open run is flushed at that primitive boundary and continues in a new window starting at the primitive's first vertex, so a surface can hold any number of vertices.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.UIDrawList.GradientVectorEmitter**: Writes a tessellated path's triangles into the draw list, each cut into the gradient's bands: measured along the line, or along the stroke over length when it is above 0.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.UIDrawList.KeptVectorEmitter**: Writes a tessellated path's triangles into the draw list, each cut to a box.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.UIDrawList.VectorEmitter**: Writes a tessellated path's triangles into the draw list, transformed and coloured.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.UIElement**: The base of every visual element: two-pass measure/arrange, layout invalidation, the owned composition , render-affecting DPs, routed events (pointer + keyboard + focus), hit-testing, and focus/capture queries. The WinUI MeasureCore/ArrangeCore seam lets layer Margin/Min/Max/alignment on top of the element's intrinsic sizing. While it is in a live tree an element listens to the brushes and the transform it shows, so a change to a shared one reaches it on the visual path, with no layout; it stops listening when it leaves, so they do not keep it alive.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.UIHost**: A per-window UI host — not a singleton, so multi-window/multi-surface is first-class. It owns the input routing and the set of roots outside the render graph, holds no engine or backend handle, and exposes the per-frame split: queue neutral events between frames, then once per frame (drain → hit-test → route → lay out) and (composite each view → ). Both run headless (no GPU), so the whole pipeline is unit-tested by queuing events and asserting DrawLists/DumpState.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.UILayer**: A screen-space compositing layer for a : sets hit-test priority (higher is on top) and is the DIP→pixel ratio (window DPI/96 for a normal overlay). In-world placement is handled externally by InWorldPanel in BinaryVibrance.Kaldra.UI.Vysara, which wraps its own UIHost with a UILayer and projects screen-space pointer events onto the panel's world-space quad — Vysara itself remains a pure 2D system.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.UIPrimKind**: The primitive family the UI compositor encodes into a draw command's — it selects the branch the single ui.slang fragment switches on. A flat so it casts to the tag cheaply. Vysara sets only a tag's low byte: a tag it emits is exactly one of these kinds, and the bits from 0x100 up are always clear. They are reserved for a host's own per-command state, which it derives into its own copy of the commands (Kaldra's painter marks a command whose texture slot holds straight-alpha texels with 0x100). A host that does so reads the kind from the low byte; on a list as Vysara hands it out, any other tag is still a broken list.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.UIRoot**: One UI surface: owns the element tree and the composition tree it composites through a pluggable . Holds no engine or backend handle, so + run to completion headless — input crosses in as a size, the product is a neutral (the headless-testable invariant).
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.UISurface**: Well-known s for the UI host. The overlay HUD is list 0; in-world surfaces take higher ids.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.UIView**: A root handle returned by : the (element + composition trees), its , and whether it is . Keep it to swap the root's content or tear it down. Non-interactive views skip hit-test/focus entirely — useful for pure composites like health bars.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.VerticalAlignment**: WinUI alignment within a layout slot's vertical axis. fills the slot.
- **BinaryVibrance.Vysara.Visibility**: WinUI element visibility. contributes zero to layout, draws nothing and never hit-tests.
